items.title: A locally finite type morphism of algebraic spaces is locally quasi-finite exactly when its field-valued fibres are discrete
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma characterising local quasi-finiteness of a locally finite type morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces by discreteness of |X_k| for every field-valued point Spec(k) -> Y (source lines 5406-5415). The easy direction reads discreteness off an etale cover; the converse is the substantive one: from a non-locally-quasi-finite U -> V one extracts a specialization u ~> u' lying over the same point v, compares the transcendence degrees d = trdeg_{kappa(v)} kappa(u) and d' = trdeg_{kappa(v)} kappa(u'), uses the scheme case of the dimension formula for specialisations to get d > d', and then shows that assuming u and u' have the same image in |X_v| produces a point r of R_v = U_v x_{X_v} U_v whose residue field is a finite separable extension of both kappa(u) and kappa(u'), forcing d = d'. That contradiction is the heart of the card and cannot be replaced by a formal argument.
